content.thinking:
I want to be careful to use placeholders rather than writing specific figures myself, tracking the alert time, onset, recovery, and duration separately. I'm also flagging a discrepancy—P1 claims the flag switched on at a certain time, but the log shows it evaluating on noticeably earlier.

I'm trying to reconcile this: the change record timestamp matches the alert time exactly, which is odd since there were no production changes in the 24 hours before onset, suggesting the flag toggle wasn't a normal deploy. I'm ruling out other causes like baseline ClientDisconnected noise and confirming the flag was off before onset, treating the ramp as starting at onset for the purposes of the writeup, and noting the mitigation involved reverting the flag.

Tracing the root cause further, the log shows a ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py line 47, likely from an empty list for shoppers without purchases that month, though that specific reading is unverified. I'm also noting contributing factors — no apparent pre-enable test coverage or error-rate gating during the flag ramp, with the error rate visible per-minute in the logs before the full outage.

Now drafting action items numbered starting at AI-3: staged flag rollout with automatic halt/rollback if error rate rises (AI-3), faster alerting on flag-correlated error spikes (AI-4), and test coverage for flag-gated paths with empty-history inputs (AI-5), tying each back to the missing rollback guard and test gap as contributing factors.

I'm also thinking through the impact summary—describing the error rate climbing from baseline to its peak while broken, and noting that affected users were shoppers with no purchases this month hitting failed account pages, with things getting progressively worse over the incident window. I want to be careful about how I reference specific file/line identifiers like spend_summary.py:47, using them sparingly and only where they're clearly log-sourced labels rather than arbitrary numbers.

action_items.item: Roll out flag-gated features in stages, and automatically halt the ramp and turn the flag off when the service's error rate rises above its baseline during the ramp.
Add a fast alert or check that watches the error rate right after a feature flag is toggled, so a flag-caused failure pages sooner than the standard paging rule.

Before a flag-gated code path can be enabled in production, require CI tests that run it with edge-case inputs, such as a shopper with purchase history but none in the current month. Run the tests added in the proposed fix in CI and confirm they fail without the fix and pass with it.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers saw account page requests fail. The error rate rose from {errors_before} before the onset to {errors_while_broken} on average while broken, peaking at {errors_at_worst}, so {errors_rise} of traffic failed that otherwise would not have. The rising series meant more shoppers hit failed account pages as the incident went on. It paged as HighErrorRate.

The failing requests raised ZeroDivisionError (division by zero) at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. These errors appear only from the onset, and they are separate from the ClientDisconnected errors that were already in the logs at baseline.

That code is the monthly spend summary, which only runs when monthly-spend-feature is on. Before the onset the flag evaluated off. At the onset it ramped to a mix of off and on, then to fully on within a minute. Reverting the flag to off ended the errors, and the metrics were back to normal at {back_to_normal}.

The flag change is the trigger. The record shows no production deploy or release in the day before the onset, so no other change coincided with it. The flag provider showed one recent flag change. The record shows no config change or rollout split either. The baseline ClientDisconnected errors were already present and do not explain the rise.

The monthly calculation divides the month's total by the count of items bought this month. Code-Fix's reading, which nothing ran and is therefore unverified, is that this list is empty for any shopper who has bought before but not this month, so the division fails. The runtime evidence shows only the exception at that line. The reason the input was empty is from the reading alone. The evidence does not show why the case was not handled or caught before the flag was enabled.

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went from partly on to fully on within about a minute, and no automatic check on error rate was seen that would halt the ramp or turn the flag off. Recovery depended on the alert and Argus's response.

Detection was not instant: the paging rule waits {rule_waits} with its condition holding before it fires. The alert came {alert_raised} after an onset of {began}, a gap of {alert_raised - began}, although the per-minute error rate was already high in the logs.
No test was seen covering the flag-on monthly path for a shopper with no purchases this month. The Code-Fix Agent had to add such tests, and they have not been run.

input.executive_summary: For a short stretch, a share of shoppers who opened their account page got an error instead of the page. The error rate was well above its usual level for {duration} and peaked at {errors_at_worst}. It began when a new monthly spending feature was switched on. The feature had a bug that made the account page fail for shoppers with no purchases in the current month. The automated responder switched the feature off, error rates returned to normal, and it then drafted a code fix, which is still waiting for review.

got_lucky: The failing path was behind a flag, so one revert removed the fault without a deploy or rollback.
Only shoppers with no purchases in the current month were affected, which limited the impact; the evidence does not show how many shoppers that was.
went_well: Argus's reading of the metrics and logs pointed straight at the flag, and the revert was applied within seconds of the investigation finishing.
The revert was judged confirmed once the service dropped below the incident's level, and the paging rule stopped firing.
A draft fix with tests was proposed right after mitigation.
went_wrong: The ramp to fully on happened with no automatic stop, so a large share of account page requests failed before anyone acted.
The paging rule's wait added to the delay between the onset and the alert.
The flag change's recorded time in the change feed is later than the onset visible in the logs, which made the timeline harder to read.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, the monthly spend-per-item calculation at spend_summary.py:47 divides by the number of items a shopper bought this month and raised ZeroDivisionError. The Code-Fix Agent's static reading (not run, so unverified) is that the list is empty for any shopper who has bought before but not this month, which is an ordinary case. The new path had no handling for it, so the account page failed for those shoppers.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for some shoppers
